## Generative AI in review, without the trade-off on security

Bringing generative AI into document review raises an obvious question: where does sensitive, privileged, and confidential data actually go? Every document sent for AI-Assisted Document Review is packaged with the user's review definition, encrypted, and sent to a designated LLM provider (Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI, depending on region) solely to generate a relevance rating and explanation. Nothing about that exchange is left to chance. Here's what the white paper covers in detail:

1

###### The full request lifecycle, from defining review criteria to submitting a job, encrypting documents for transmission, and returning ratings to the document viewer, spans a fully mapped, auditable technical architecture.

2

###### LLM providers never store queries, responses, or client data, and have no direct user access or interface into Reveal Enterprise systems; access happens exclusively through Reveal Enterprise APIs.

3

###### Reveal's AI Pledge extends to this feature specifically: user definitions, documents, and responses are retained within the client project only, and are never reused to update Reveal's or the LLM provider's AI models.

4

###### LLM providers run fully automated abuse monitoring with zero data retention, meaning no human ever manually inspects your queries or documents, even for accounts flagged by automated detection.

### TLS 1.2/1.3

Encryption standard protecting every query and response exchanged with the LLM provider, in transit

### 0

Instances of client data used to train Reveal's or the LLM provider's AI models, per Reveal's AI Pledge

### 100%

LLM providers supported by region (Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI), each governed by the same data protections

## Get the full white paper: AI-Assisted Document Review, Security & Data Privacy

A complete technical and policy breakdown of how Reveal AI's AI-Assisted Document Review feature handles your data, for security teams, privacy officers, and legal buyers evaluating generative AI in eDiscovery. This white paper includes:

### How the AI-Assisted Document Review architecture works end-to-end, from defining relevancy criteria to secure transmission and rating delivery.

### Exactly what data the LLM provider can and can't access, including logging practices, encryption standards, and why AWS and GCP never share logs with the LLM providers themselves.

### How Reveal's AI Pledge applies to generative AI features, and what "never used to train AI models" actually means in practice.

### How automated abuse monitoring works without human review, including what happens if a potential policy violation is flagged.

[Download the White Paper](https://www.revealdata.com/guides/ai-assisted-document-review-security-data-privacy#announcementClose)
